column1: # BASE/icon2bc contiguous decoder-state ownership pass, checkpoint 06409a9

column5: Separate verified statics; setup folds offset+entry into ECX and loop reloads destination. This remains the retained checkpoint.
An inline reader returning the command still emitted source=EAX/command=ECX; an inline return boundary alone is not the missing abstraction.
One flat 0x44-byte record preserves every retail relocation address/addend, but broad alias and declaration-state changes regress setup/decoder allocation.

The flat record plus the retail destination lifetime uniquely recovers source=ECX, command=EAX, and count=EDX. It keeps X=EBX and destination=ESI, exactly the reverse of retail, and adds one relocation occurrence.
A two-pointer record at 0x534cd4 groups only destination/source. It is too narrow to trigger command ownership and emits source=EAX/command=ECX/count=EBX/destination=EDX.
A contiguous record for destination/source/shadow-count/X0/color/run at 0x534cd4..0x534ceb remains source=EAX/command=ECX/count=EBX/destination=EDX.
Byte-offset setup recovers 13*frame=EBX and X=ESI, but colors entry.x=EDI/entry=ECX and flips the decoder back to source=EAX/command=ECX/count=EBX/destination=EDX.
Declaring the typed entry before its x/srcOffset snapshots folds offset+data into ECX and retains the wrong decoder coloring.
Mutating formal x preserves source=ECX/command=EAX/count=EDX but still leaves X=EBX/destination=ESI and broadly regresses setup.
Nesting the tail command record inside the full state changes compiler state enough to recover X=ESI, but loses command/count ownership and leaves destination=EDX.
Moving the same flat record to a TU-private header after Misc perturbs the prologue/row lifetime broadly and does not recover the retail register chain.
